history.dynasty: Cholas (11th century origins); later expansions by the Vijayanagara Empire (Achutaraya Nayak) with Pallava-era renovations
history.summary: One of the 108 Divya Desams and among the most celebrated Vaishnavite temples of Tamil Nadu, located in Vishnu Kanchi (Chinna Kanchipuram). The moolavar is Varadaraja Perumal in a standing posture facing west, under the Punyakoti Vimanam; the temple also enshrines Perundevi Thayar in a separate shrine, and the Athi Varadhar idol (made of Athi/fig wood) is brought out for public worship once every 40 years (last darshan 2019). The complex is an amalgam of embellishments over centuries, with contributions from the Cholas, Pallavas and Vijayanagara rulers. Legend: when Brahma performed a yajna here, Vishnu emerged from the flames of the fire; when Brahma's consort Saraswati flooded the site as the Vegavati river, Vishnu lay in a reclining posture to halt the flood. Glorified in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham by Tirumangai Alvar, Bhoothathazhwar and Peyalvar. name: Varadaraja Perumal Temple
town_description: Kancheepuram (Kanchipuram), about 75 km southwest of Chennai, is one of India's seven sacred cities and is famed as the 'city of a thousand temples', home to 15 Divya Desams, the Shaivite Ekambaranathar and Kamakshi Amman temples, and its renowned handloom silk sarees.

travel.airport: Chennai International Airport (MAA), about 75 km away, is the nearest airport; Tiruchirappalli is a farther alternative.
travel.railway: Kanchipuram railway station on the Chengalpattu-Arakkonam line; Chennai (75 km) is the nearest major rail hub.
travel.road: On the Chennai-Bangalore highway (NH-48) corridor, reachable via the Chennai-Chengalpattu route; the temple is on South/West Mada Street in Chinna Kanchipuram, with regular buses from Chennai, Bengaluru and nearby towns.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; May-June for the Vaikasi Brahmotsavam festival crowd.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources disagree: 6:00 AM-12:30 PM and 3:30-8:30 PM (redbus, hindu-blog) vs 6:00-11:00 AM and 4:00-8:00 PM (templefolks) vs 6:30 AM-12:00 noon and 4:00-8:00 PM (vardhmanvacations) - verify before visiting.
